answer.reason: The verses tell of Jael sheltering Sisera and then killing him, and showing his body to Barak, which add to the summary's bare relation.

clauses.english: took Sisera into her tent when he fled and covered him
clauses.quote: Turn in, my lord, turn in to me; fear not.

clauses.english: drove a tent nail into the temples of the sleeping Sisera, and he died
clauses.quote: smote the nail into his temples, and fastened it into the ground

doubts: JDG 5:6 mentions the days of Jael only as a time reference, so it was left out.
JDG 5:24 is a blessing pronounced on her, not an event, so it was left out.
The second clause restates the summary's 'killer of Sisera' as the deed itself, as the rules allow.
